chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi narrated from Ali ibn Mukhallad al-Ayyadi, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Amari (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me that: Abu Tahir ibn Bilal performed Hajj and saw Ali ibn Ja'far spending great expenditures. When he returned, he wrote about that to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), and it appeared in his reply: 'We had ordered him to take one hundred thousand dinars, then we ordered him to take the like of it, but he refused to accept it, keeping it for us. What is for people to enter into our matter regarding what we have not included them in?' He said: And he entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him), and he ordered him to take thirty thousand dinars.

key_terms.إِبْقَاءً عَلَيْنَا: Keeping it for us (preserving their wealth)

ai.seo_question: What is the story behind Ali ibn Ja'far's refusal of the Imams' financial gifts?
ai.summary: This narrative from Kitab al-Ghayba highlights the financial status and generosity of Ali ibn Ja'far (a.s.) by recounting how Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) and later Imam al-Askari (a.s.) repeatedly offered him large sums of money, which he initially refused to preserve their wealth. It illustrates the concept of the Imam's authority over the finances of his close relatives and the etiquette of not interfering in their affairs, specifically noting the unique privilege of the Ahl al-Bayt to manage their own resources without external interference. The refusal to accept funds was an act of preserving the Imam's treasury, demonstrating the deep spiritual and economic bond between the Imams and their family.
